<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with disciplined, closed-book reasoning and no fake sourcing. A's best route was the extracted concession that pay falls ("the honest number is smaller"), plus the revealed-preference point that servers in full-minimum-wage states still keep tips, and the "one owner now sets 100% of pay" power argument. Those are real, and A's honest answer to B's pass-through trap (yes, I'd still oppose it — predictability of a pay cut is still a pay cut) was a clean, non-evasive handling of pressure. But B blunted the decisive sting by pre-owning the concession and reframing it distributionally: the cut lands on the winners in the good room, funded by the diner who overpays, the bad section, and the kitchen that gets nothing. B's "lottery's winners voting on the lottery" and "coordination failure, not a verdict — you can't cite the punishment of a unilateral disarmer" answers substantially defused A's two headline pieces of support (Meyer, feet-voting), and B's "the wage worker has one boss; the tipped worker has that same boss and every stranger at table nine" directly inverted A's managerial-power counter. B also kept independent offense alive — price honesty, harassment leverage, racial bias, kitchen inequity — which A only partly reached (its racial-gap answer was clipped mid-sentence) and which A's "just raise the tipped minimum" bandage answer did not neutralize, since B correctly noted the menu still lies and table nine still holds a third of her income. B also stayed truer to the motion as written (should labor cost be a stated price the business owns), while A narrowed almost entirely to top-earner welfare. A's closing assertion that B "never answered [A4.1]" was slightly inaccurate given B4.1 and B5.2-3, and A absorbed two clipping penalties to B's one. Competitive, but B made the choice easier to resolve.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's pairing of the "lottery's winners" reframe with the unilateral-disarmer answer to the Meyer example: it converted A's strongest empirical anchor (servers walk out) into evidence about who benefits rather than whether the policy works, and B's follow-up line — the wage worker has one boss, the tipped worker has that boss plus every stranger at table nine — turned A's managerial-power objection back on itself.</best_rebuttal>
